clue.text: A container that's not properly shut

parts.note: a jar is a container for food or liquids

explanation.surface: A box or tub whose lid has been left loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left slightly open is ajar, never quite closed.

clue.text: Handbook shows a piece coated with resin

indicators.note: something coated with a substance is surrounded by it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: lac is a resin secreted by insects, used in shellac
a man is a piece in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A guide shows a component varnished with resin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' is a chess man, which LAC encloses after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is a yearly reference book of facts and data.

clue.text: Savings account written up as something worth having

indicators.note: in a down clue, written up means written from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: TESSA was a British tax-exempt special savings account

explanation.surface: A savings account described as a valuable possession.
explanation.walkthrough: TESSA was a 1990s British tax-free savings scheme; written up in this down entry it appears backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is any useful or valuable thing or quality.

clue.text: Reverse of jolly character

indicators.note: the instruction to turn round the little word that follows it, read backwards

parts.note: a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: A gloomy personality, the opposite of a cheerful one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' turns 'of' into FO; 'jolly' is not cheerful but a Royal Marine (RM). The surface invites an antonym of jolly, which leads nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Form can mean someone's nature or disposition, as in 'true to form', so it stands for character.

clue.text: Dreadful experience of French exam is overwhelming

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A French exam that proves overwhelming and awful.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful trial or harrowing experience.

clue.text: Males try desperately to appear so!

definitions.text: Males try desperately to appear so!

indicators.note: acting desperately means flailing wildly, so these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Men strain to look commanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperately' rearranges MALES TRY; 'so' at the end points to the answer, making the whole clue the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Masterly means showing the skill of a master, which men might strain to display.

clue.text: Pink belt

definitions.meaning: to pink is for an engine to make a metallic rattling from early ignition
to belt is to hit hard

explanation.definitionFit: Engine knocking is called pinking, and a knock is also a blow or hit.

clue.text: To be a greengrocer, one must have expertise

definitions.text: To be a greengrocer, one must have expertise

parts.words: To be a greengrocer, one must have expertise
parts.note: an idiom for being skilled is read literally as being an expert on a vegetable a greengrocer sells

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be thoroughly expert in one's field, and literally suits a vegetable seller.

clue.text: Reserve troops are not dressed

parts.note: dressing ranks means lining up soldiers straight; troops held in reserve are not standing in the formation

explanation.definitionFit: Being off the straight row of a drill formation means misaligned, and figuratively improper.

clue.text: Russian supporting friendly relations

indicators.note: in a down clue, a supporting word sits underneath the other

parts.note: kind means friendly
Red was a common label for a Soviet Russian

explanation.surface: A Russian backing amicable ties between nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' places RED below KIND in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred means one's relatives, family members collectively.

clue.text: A part of geese I'd processed?

definitions.text: A part of geese I'd processed?

indicators.note: processed food has been worked over, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A foie-gras maker admits turning goose parts into food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'processed' rearranges A PART OF GEESE I'D; the whole clue also describes the food.
explanation.definitionFit: This French delicacy is a paste made from fattened goose liver, which is part of a goose processed.

clue.text: Yellowish-brown dirt covering lead

indicators.note: one word wraps around the other, as a coat covers what is under it

parts.note: mud is wet dirt
the lead in a play or film is its star

explanation.surface: Grime spread over a yellowish-brown metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the metal, but means the leading performer; 'covering' has dirt wrapping round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mustard names a dull yellowish-brown colour, like the condiment.

clue.text: Contract made by South and North, unexpectedly overcoming East

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south

indicators.note: to overcome is to get on top of and envelop, so one piece is put around the other
something happening unexpectedly comes out of the expected order, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A bridge contract bid by the South and North players, who surprisingly beat East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' jumbles NORTH to HORTN, and 'overcoming' wraps that round E to give HORTEN after S. The bridge picture makes 'Contract' look like a noun; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract something is to make it smaller or briefer, which is to cut it down.

clue.text: Take Metro with dean, perhaps, to see this cathedral

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the words may be rearranged into something other than what they say

explanation.surface: Ride the Paris Metro with a churchman to visit a famous cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the letters of METRO and DEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre-Dame is the great Gothic cathedral in Paris.

clue.text: Tender put out to sea from Queen Elizabeth

parts.note: a ship that has put out to sea is off, away from shore
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is Queen Elizabeth's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A small boat tender leaving from the liner Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' suggests a ship's boat, matching the liner, but here it is a verb meaning to present.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender a payment or resignation is to put it forward, which is to propose it formally.

clue.text: Soundly crush nut

indicators.note: soundly signals that the word is used for how it is spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: to crush an enemy is to conquer it

explanation.surface: Smash a nut thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: A conker is the shiny horse-chestnut used in a British children's game where one is swung on a string at another's.
explanation.definitionFit: A conker is the seed of the horse chestnut, loosely called a nut.

clue.text: Looking back regretfully at closing variety

indicators.note: a variety is a different arrangement, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Feeling wistful at the closing of a variety theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' rearranges AT CLOSING; the surface's music-hall closure evokes the very feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgic means wistfully yearning for the past.

clue.text: American singer having miserable time

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling miserable
bird is British slang for a prison sentence, time inside

explanation.surface: A US vocalist going through a wretched period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' means a songbird, not a vocalist. Doing bird, from rhyming slang 'birdlime' for time, is British slang for serving a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: The bluebird is a North American thrush noted for its song.

clue.text: Coastline seen from quarters on ship

parts.note: S and E, south and east, are two quarters of the compass
aboard means on a ship

explanation.surface: Viewing the shore from a cabin at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' looks like cabins but means compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: The seaboard is land bordering the sea, a shore region.

clue.text: Come across and record deliveries

parts.note: a gramophone record is a disc
in cricket an over is a set of six balls delivered by one bowler

explanation.surface: Stumble upon something, and keep a record of bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is cricket's unit of six deliveries bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: To come across something is to find it by chance, as an explorer does.

clue.text: Noise level of CD ie, adjusted to be loud, initially

indicators.note: adjusted letters are moved into new positions

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word loud

explanation.surface: Turn a CD's volume up to make it loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusted' rearranges CD IE into DECI.
explanation.definitionFit: A decibel is the unit measuring sound intensity, how loud something is.

clue.text: Businessman is very convincing

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
a gent is a gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A trader who persuades very effectively.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'Businessman' must be split in two, business and man, each giving its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A cogent argument is forceful and persuasive, leaving little room for doubt.

clue.text: Beat time right for American singer

parts.note: to tan a hide is to beat it
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Keep the rhythm properly for a US vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singer' is a songbird again; 'Beat time' looks like keeping the rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: The tanager is a brightly coloured American songbird.

clue.text: Commercial money-changing is slow

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
agio is the charge or premium for exchanging currency

explanation.surface: The advert's foreign exchange business is sluggish.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical direction for a leisurely tempo.

clue.text: In church, has to do some engraving

indicators.note: in places the word that follows inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
taken as written

explanation.surface: A church has to carry out some decorative carving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals a container; CE, the Church of England, is the usual crossword abbreviation for church.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase metal is to engrave or emboss a design on it.

clue.text: Sport seen in equestrian venue

definitions.meaning: a racket game played with a shuttlecock
the country estate in Gloucestershire that hosts a famous annual horse trials

explanation.surface: A game being played at a horse-riding event.
explanation.definitionFit: The shuttlecock game took its name from the Duke of Beaufort's estate, which now hosts the three-day eventing championship.

clue.text: Committee that needs real power like this

indicators.note: the run of letters is needed from, and sits within, the two words before it

explanation.surface: A weak committee requires genuine authority to act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' signals letters drawn from within 'Committee that'; 'like this' is a link pointing at the result. Having teeth is an idiom for real force.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving a body teeth idiomatically means granting it real force to enforce decisions.

clue.text: Paddy swears by it

parts.note: Paddy is a nickname for an Irishman, and this is the mild oath he is stereotyped as uttering

explanation.definitionFit: The Irish exclamation is a minced form of 'by God', an oath.

clue.text: Drinks English and Chinese medicine

parts.note: gins are drinks of spirit

explanation.surface: Gin and a remedy from China, served together.
explanation.definitionFit: The root of this plant is a traditional Chinese tonic remedy.

clue.text: Catches salmon that's been preserved, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: lox is smoked or cured salmon

explanation.surface: An angler lands salmon that will be smoked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catches' looks like fishing but means fastenings.
explanation.definitionFit: Locks are fastenings, as are catches on a door or box.

clue.text: Vessel at Land's End, in what condition?

indicators.note: the end of the word land is its last letter

parts.note: how asks what state something is in, as in 'how is he?'

explanation.surface: A ship off Cornwall's westernmost point, its state unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land's End' is the tip of Cornwall, but here it means the last letter of 'Land'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhow is an Arab sailing boat with a lateen sail.

clue.text: I must quit academic post to become cleaner

indicators.note: quitting means leaving, so the letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: a chair is a professorship

explanation.surface: A professor who must give up the job to become a cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: A char, or charwoman, is British for a domestic cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A char is a woman hired to clean a house or office.
